title: AI services you can sell
lede: Start with your niche, then choose a service that solves a problem they will pay to fix.
deliverable: A suitable agency service and real examples to investigate for the chosen niche.
body:
You do not need to start with a blank page. These are services I would look at first. Start with a niche you understand, have worked in or can get access to. Then look at the problems those businesses have and which of these services would be worth paying for.

Start with the niche

If you already know an industry, use that. You will understand the owner, the work and the language faster. If you have no niche yet, ask Jarvis to help you compare a few. The service comes from the problem you find, not from picking an automation at random.

Help me research [niche] in [location], find the problems worth paying to solve and match them to suitable agency services with real examples.

Study the agency offer

Study what an agency offers to install or manage for a client. A software company’s customer story can show a useful result, but it does not prove that an agency is selling that service successfully. You can take the same service into a different niche, a different location or a problem the current offer does not cover well. Keep the useful idea and make the offer your own.

Heavy advertising is a useful demand signal and gives you angles to test quickly. It does not tell you the advertiser’s profit. Look at the service, the promise, the customer examples and how you would deliver it.

These services can support a $20k-a-month agency. That depends on your price, number of clients and delivery costs. Websites are a simple place to start; reaching $10k a month is possible, while scaling further usually needs higher-value builds, recurring work or a team.

1. AI receptionist

What you sell. An AI phone agent that answers when the team cannot, takes the caller’s details and books suitable jobs or appointments. The business keeps its number. Missed and after-hours calls forward to the agent, which checks the calendar and sends the team a summary.

Who to sell it to. Any business that takes customer calls. Think trades, clinics, salons and other local businesses. Start with one type so the questions, bookings and demo are easy to understand.

See an existing provider or customer example

What to show. A caller rings the demo number, asks about a service and gets the correct next step. Show a booking and a question that needs a human.

We help local trade businesses turn missed calls into booked jobs with an AI receptionist that answers when their team cannot.

2. AI appointment-setting agency

What you sell. You install and manage the follow-up that turns enquiries into booked consultations. The client gets the system set up around their service, connected to their calendar and looked after by you. They are paying for the work and the result, not just a software login.

Who to sell it to. Start with one niche where consultations lead to valuable sales. The business needs enough enquiries and staff available to take the appointments. If you also generate the enquiries with ads, that is a bigger service to deliver.

A live agency offer. SyncPro Media sells a dental-implant system combining Meta ads, AI follow-up and consultation booking. Its page advertises a $40K sales target in 40 days with continued free work if missed. That is its advertised promise, not a result I have independently checked. Study the offer and what they deliver; do not copy the target without the ability to deliver it.

What to show. Submit a test enquiry. Show the follow-up, qualification questions and appointment reaching the right calendar.

We build and run the follow-up system that turns your dental enquiries into booked implant consultations, so your team can focus on treatment sales.

3. Old-lead and unsold-quote recovery

What you sell. Reconnect with people who enquired or received a quote but never bought. The system follows up, handles agreed questions and brings interested buyers back to the sales team. It tracks which opportunities become paid work.

Who to sell it to. Businesses with a useful old database or unsold quotes. Roofers, builders, clinics and home-improvement companies often already have the opportunity sitting in their CRM.

An agency selling it. Mixed Media Ventures provides managed database-reactivation campaigns for clients and reseller agencies. Its roofing case reports 127 qualified appointments over 90 days. The roofer is unnamed and the figures are agency-reported. This supports the service category; it does not prove our example’s five-paid-job target.

What to show. Show an eligible old enquiry, the follow-up conversation and the sales-team handoff. Then show where the eventual sale would be recorded.

We’ll get your roofing company 5 more jobs in 30 days from unsold estimates, or we work for free.

4. Outbound appointment-setting agency

What you sell. You find suitable prospects, write and run the outreach, manage replies and book qualified sales conversations for the client. You build the system in their accounts and keep improving it while their team handles sales.

Who to sell it to. A B2B business with a clear offer and someone able to take sales calls. Start with your chosen niche, then check whether there are enough reachable buyers and whether a sale is worth the cost of getting the meeting.

A live agency offer and client example. ColdIQ’s managed implementation builds and runs outbound in accounts the client owns. It also sells software, so use this service page rather than the software homepage. Its Hemlane case explains targeting active rental-property owners and reports a 5.5% reply rate. That is an agency-reported campaign result, not proof for a commercial-cleaning offer.

What to show. Show the target account, relevant outreach, a reply and the handoff to the client’s sales calendar. Finding contacts alone is not the finished service.

We find your ideal customers, start the conversations and book qualified sales calls for your team.

5. Custom AI CRM

What you sell. Build a CRM around how the business actually works. Enquiries, quotes, jobs, documents and follow-ups sit together, with agreed tasks automated. Decide what it replaces and what it connects to before you quote.

Who to sell it to. Established businesses whose team keeps copying information between spreadsheets, inboxes and software. The owner wants fewer things falling through the cracks and a clear view of each job.

What to show. Show one job moving from enquiry to quote and delivery in the same record. Show who updates it and what the team no longer needs to copy.

We build one CRM around your business so your team stops re-entering information and chasing job updates.

My recommendation: use AI arbitrage for this one. A custom CRM is more difficult and technical than it looks. Get an experienced developer to review the requirements and scope the build before you quote the client. You manage the client and delivery; the developer handles the build.

6. AI website agency

What you sell. Build websites for businesses that have no useful site or an outdated one. AI helps with the layout, copy and build. You organise their services, photos, contact details and enquiry flow into a site they can actually use.

Who to sell it to. Local businesses whose current site makes it hard to understand the service or request a quote. Trades, clinics and professional services are easy starting points.

What to show. Open the site as a customer on a phone. Find the service, view the work and submit a test enquiry that reaches the business.

We build local businesses a professional website that makes it easy for customers to understand the service and request a quote.

7. AI content engine and editing

What you sell. Turn the client’s footage and ideas into a regular supply of edited reels, captions and other content. AI helps with scripts, cuts and captions. You check the edits and send a consistent batch for approval.

Who to sell it to. Business owners, creators and brands that need content but cannot keep up with planning and editing. Start with one format and a clear monthly output.

What to show. Show the raw footage beside one finished edit, then the batch ready for the client’s approval. Be clear on how much content and how many revisions they get.

We turn your raw footage into a regular supply of edited videos, ready for you to approve and post.

8. A niche AI automation agency

What you sell. Choose a type of business and offer a free AI audit. Find where the team loses time, money or opportunities. Recommend the most valuable first fix, show what it would do and sell the implementation. The audit opens the conversation; the build is the paid service.

Who to sell it to. Owners who know AI could help but do not know what to implement. Speak to one business type so each conversation teaches you more about the same workflows.

How you find the paid project. Have the owner show you a real workflow: what starts it, who handles it, where they copy information and what happens when it gets delayed. Put a cost on the problem, check the proposed fix with your developer, then show the client what you would implement. Quoting, document collection and invoice follow-up are possibilities to investigate, not ready-made offers to assume they need.

An agency example. LeftClick advertises custom automation, CRM work, onboarding and reporting, with a diagnostic call before the project. Use it to study the service model; it does not validate our previous electrical-quoting example.

What to show. Walk through a real task with the owner, identify the problem and show the proposed fix. You quote that implementation after checking it with the delivery person.

Know you need AI but not where to start? We’ll audit your business for free and show you the first thing we would automate.

These are offer examples to adapt. Set your target, timing and guarantee around what you can deliver. A straightforward receptionist setup can take 2 to 5 working days once the details and access are ready. Start with one niche, identify a worthwhile problem and use Jarvis to develop the service and offer together.
